subject: an iron longsword inventory item icon for an ARPG loot grid
bestPrompt: Stylized hand-painted ARPG inventory loot icon of a plain cold iron longsword, single hero object angled diagonally about 35 degrees corner to corner, blade tip toward upper-right, scaled large to fill the square loot-grid cell frame. Bold painterly digital illustration in the flat, saturated, punchy high-contrast finish of Diablo IV and Path of Exile 2 weapon icons — confident visible brushwork, hand-crafted icon craft, absolutely NOT a photoreal 3D render, NOT a flat vector emoji, NOT a smooth sticker, NOT a cel-shaded gradient blob, NOT a flat grey color blob. Forged iron blade with hard beveled steel: one crisp bright cool-white specular edge line catches the light down the top bevel and central fuller ridge, the opposite bevel drops to deep near-black core shadow — a clear light-bevel vs dark-bevel split for a full black-to-white value range, NOT a flat mid-grey gradient. Hammered planished facets, diagonal grind lines, pitted worn iron, chipped edge nicks, temper mottling. Aged dark-brown wrapped-leather grip with distinct painted coils, blackened iron crossguard with crisp edges, a sharply engraved beveled iron disc pommel with one bright rivet glint — every sub-form crisp at icon scale. Controlled top-left key light. Cleanly separated from a flat dark charcoal background. Crisp silhouette, rich hammered-iron material, high detail, extreme contrast. No purple, no magic glow, no rim halo, no orange wash, no text, no watermark, no border, no low-poly, no muddy midtones.
technique: On Lucid Origin the winning stack is: (1) anti-flat painterly anchoring — name Diablo IV / Path of Exile 2 icon craft plus 'confident visible brushwork' AND a full anti-default negative chain ('NOT a photoreal 3D render, NOT a flat vector emoji, NOT a smooth sticker, NOT a cel-shaded gradient blob, NOT a flat grey color blob') to fight the model's flat cel default; (2) a diagonal ~35-degree corner-to-corner hero pose that fills the square cell (near-vertical reads as a thin object that wastes the frame and scores lower); (3) achromatic HAMMERED micro-texture (planished facets, grind lines, pitting, edge nicks) instead of colored lighting drama — this is what lifts materialRendering. Critically, keep the lighting language austere: any 'off-screen window / sky reflection' phrasing makes Lucid Origin paint a purple/lavender enchant bloom, and 'warm rim light' produces an unmotivated orange halo — both get docked as unintended magic cues. Ask for a plain light-bevel-vs-dark-bevel split and a single cool specular edge line, nothing more.

iterations.note: Prior gpt-image-2 winner ported to Lucid Origin: painterly D4/PoE2 + full lighting recipe + 35deg diagonal. Solid material (70) but the warm 'bounce/rim light' rendered as a yellow-orange halo along the blade edge — judge read it as an unintended enchant glow and docked edge/value.

Killed the warm halo and went near-vertical with only a cool specular. Halo gone but blade collapsed to flat uniform mid-grey (material 56) and the radial vignette competed with the object. Vertical thin pose under-filled the cell.

Tried split lighting via an 'off-screen window specular reflection'. Lucid Origin turned the reflection into a large purple/lavender bloom at mid-fuller — an unintended magic cue on a plain-iron item; cleanliness fell to 80.

BEST-tier. Dropped all colored reflection language: 'purely achromatic steel greys, ZERO color tint' + heavy HAMMERED micro-texture (planished facets, grind lines, pitting, nicks). Cleanliness 95, styleCohesion 74. Diagonal fill despite asking near-vertical.

Regression. Re-added cool-blue + warm-amber temperature contrast AND forced near-vertical centered pose. Blade went flat/chalky again and the thin vertical object wasted the frame — judge explicitly wanted the tighter angled fill back.

Winner (ties gen 4, cleaner recipe). Gen-4 achromatic hammered base + explicit light-bevel-vs-dark-bevel specular split + sharply defined pommel/guard sub-forms, back on the 35deg diagonal frame-fill. Same near-ceiling dims: silhouette 78, edge 72, style 70, cleanliness 95; material still capped 66.

ceilingVerdict: Model-capped at ~68 for this subject via prompt alone. Composition levers are effectively maxed (silhouette 78, cleanliness 95, styleCohesion ~72), but Lucid Origin will not paint crisp specular hotspots or hammered micro-relief onto a large flat blade face — across 6 gens materialRendering never cleared 70 and valueHierarchy never cleared 68, the judge consistently calling the blade a 'flat wash / color blob'. Reaching 90 would need a different lever than prompt text: a metal-heavy LoRA/style-reference image, img2img/ControlNet from a real forged-steel reference, or post-gen relight — not more prompt tokens.
